messages:
Ada (eng-runtime): Quick thought — the current lease handoff is fragile during reshuffles. If a node dies between tombstone write and claim we end up with temporary no-owner windows.
Ben (eng-runtime): Agreed. We've seen a couple of flaps in canaries. What's the simplest stronger guarantee we can aim for?
Clara (eng-runtime): Two cheap guarantees: (1) never observe two owners at once, (2) make takeover fast (sub-second) and idempotent.
Ada (eng-runtime): Proposal: move to a two-phase epoched claim with an append-only transfer-log per-prefix. Owner writes `TRANSFER: intent, epoch=N+1`, target reads the intent and attempts claim by writing `CLAIM: epoch=N+2` atomically. sequencer increments epoch.
Ben (eng-runtime): That sounds like extra writes — what's the perf hit at hot prefixes?
Clara (eng-runtime): We only do it on reshuffle, not on every access. Hot steady-state still uses local lease. Transfer path is rare and can be optimized with short-circuit checks.
Dave (eng-sre): How do we clean up failed intents? If a process crashes after writing TRANSFER, who garbage collects?
Ada (eng-runtime): Add TTL + sequencer-based lease expiration. If target doesn't finish claim within T, sequencer can advance epoch and allow another candidate. Also include a `last_seen_node` metadata for debugging.
Emily (eng-platform): We need metrics for transfer latencies, TRANSFER->CLAIM success rate, and number of orphan intents. Add labels: prefix_hash, source_node, target_node, epoch.
reshuffle-bot: deploy scheduled: canary reshuffle test at 2918203300 — results will be posted in #eng-runtime.
Ben (eng-runtime): Test plan idea: simulate concurrent claims with a small harness. Steps: 1) pick prefix P, 2) start 3 claimers, 3) kill owner mid-transfer, 4) assert at most one final owner and no double-accept.
Clara (eng-runtime): Edge case: simultaneous sequencer partitions where two sequencers think they can advance epoch. We must gate epoch advance behind a centralized monoponic counter (sequencer or RAFT).
Ada (eng-runtime): Right. Rely on sequencer's strong monotonicity. If cluster partitions, transfer should stall not split ownership. That means fallback reads may hit stale owner — fallback policy must accept stale reads until takeover completes.
Dave (eng-sre): Operationally, how will this manifest? Alerts for long TRANSFER lifetimes and orphan counts. Also a runbook: `if orphan_count > 10` then trigger `reshuffle-age` sweep job.
Emily (eng-platform): We should add a small on-disk marker for transfers so a node reboot can resume. Something like `/var/lib/runtime/transfer_<prefix>.json`.
Ada (eng-runtime): Pseudocode for claim step: ```
# target node
if read_owner(prefix).epoch == N and read_transfer(prefix).epoch == N+1:
  write_claim(prefix, epoch=N+2, claimer=node_id)
  verify_owner(prefix) == node_id
else:
  abort
```
Ben (eng-runtime): What about eviction interplay? If we demote a prefix concurrently with a transfer, we must ensure eviction doesn't drop KV state mid-handshake. Maybe transfers pin residency until claim completes.
Clara (eng-runtime): Agree — add a `transfer_pin` flag that increments residency refcount during transfer. Pin is removed after successful CLAIM or after TTL expiration.
Dave (eng-sre): TTLs need conservative defaults in prod but shorter in canaries. Also add a metric for pinned bytes to catch leaks.
Ada (eng-runtime): Security note: claims should be authenticated (signed by node key) so a compromised node can't forge claims and steal prefixes.
Emily (eng-platform): For private deployments, KMS sign/verify might be required. Add an opt-in config `claims.signed=true`.
Ben (eng-runtime): Okay next action items: Ada to draft a lightweight RFC with the transfer-log format + state diagram. Clara to own sequencer gating requirements. Dave to add monitoring knobs. Emily will prototype on-disk resume.
Ada (eng-runtime): I'll add a minimal test harness and include the chaos scenarios (node crash, sequencer failover, clock skew). Expect RFC by EOW.
Clara (eng-runtime): Thanks — also include an offline validation tool that scans transfer logs and asserts epoch monotonicity per prefix.
Ben (eng-runtime): small nit: keep transfer-log entries compact (binary protobuf) to avoid IO spike on mass reshuffles.
Ada (eng-runtime): Good call. We'll add compression + batched fsyncs.
Dave (eng-sre): I'll draft runbook snippets for the sweeper job.
Emily (eng-platform): I'll add metric docs and a Grafana panel mockup.
Ada (eng-runtime): Thanks all. We'll follow up after RFC. :thumbsup:
